title.narrative: Resilient and Flourishing Communities in Dethwok & Lul Payam of Fashoda County

description.narrative: Lul and Dethwok payams of Fashoda County in Upper Nile State were heavily affected by the violence of the last months of 2022. The population in Lul payam fled the area amidst killings, torturing and rape. Severe gender-based violence violations were committed. Dethwok payam was not directly reached by the violence but the inhabitants fled when fighting came close. After a military intervention by the Central Government in December 2022, fighting stopped in Fashoda County. At the beginning of 2023 the local population gradually started to go back to their home areas in Dethwok and Lul payams. However, the returnees face several challenges. Dethwok Payam of Fashoda has 10 Bomas (Ashak, Coshang, Alel, Dethwok, Othurshok, Pabiew, Borbak, Malo, Abenyai, and Atar) with an estimate population of 800 HHs (estimated 4,800 individuals) after recent displacement. According to the community leaders and local authorities in Dethwok Payam, most of the community was displaced to Kodok town and some to Melut County. Currently, the community is voluntarily returning to Dethwok Payam. The area is surrounded by floodwater, with Dethwok St. Ambrose catholic church is on Island where there are no sanitation facilities or protected water sources for people to use. Lul payam falls in the southern part of Kodok town in Fashoda County. Lul payam has 13 Bomas. They are Nyingar, Bol, Boodh, Pabur, Beew, Yony, Lul, Abaneem, Agot, Thworlong, Kwom, Wadman and Agwor. The Estimate Population of Lul payam is 24,360 individuals (4,060HH). Some of these people got displaced to Malakal and Kodok during the recent clashes in November and December 2022. However, many of them have started to return to their villages and they are in dire need of support to rebuild their lives and livelihoods,
